name: I G Petrochemicals Ltd
tagline: India's largest phthalic-anhydride maker and only maleic-anhydride producer, near the bottom of a brutal commodity down-cycle (ROCE ~3%, ~1.1x book) - with the PAN anti-dumping duty just extended for 5 years and a plasticiser plant starting up; a cyclical-recovery bet, not a structural compounder
business_overview: IGPL manufactures Phthalic Anhydride (PAN - ~90% of revenue; used in plasticisers, paints, unsaturated polyester resins, CPC pigments), Maleic Anhydride (MAN - the only Indian producer, made near-free from PAN wash-water) and Benzoic Acid. It is India's largest PAN producer (~50%+ of domestic capacity, world #2), a virtual domestic duopoly with Thirumalai (plus new unlisted entrant KLJ). A plasticiser plant is being commissioned (expected to contribute from Q2 FY27).
fundamentals_table: 5-yr sales growth ~11%; earnings highly erratic (OPM swings 5-22%)
At/near the bottom - PAN-orthoxylene spreads near the ~$85/ton conversion cost; MAN priced ~30% below PAN vs +10-15% historically (Chinese oversupply)
Modest leverage; dividend payout ~260% (maintained through the downturn)
~1.1x book, ~19x depressed earnings (at FY18 peak ROCE 35%+ the stock traded ~3.5x book); 'blockbuster' Q1 FY27 profit reported (partly crude/inventory-driven)
fundamentals_narrative: This is a textbook commodity-cycle-trough setup. IGPL is the lowest-cost domestic PAN producer with a byproduct MAN stream at near-zero marginal cost, but PAN-OX spreads have collapsed to conversion cost and MAN prices are depressed by Chinese exports (China has not enforced its single-use-plastics rules, so MAN is being dumped internationally). Return ratios are therefore near zero. Three things could turn it: (1) the anti-dumping duty on PAN has been EXTENDED for 5 years (confirmed Aug 2026) - structurally positive for domestic players; (2) the new plasticiser plant starts contributing from Q2 FY27 (currently the company bears its depreciation/interest with no offsetting revenue); (3) no new domestic PAN capacity is expected for 1-2 years and competitor Thirumalai is over-levered on a delayed US MAN project. A spread recovery plus the plasticiser ramp could multiply earnings off this low base and re-rate the stock from ~1.1x toward 2.5-3x book.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Trades near book value, oscillating with crude/PAN-OX spreads; a 'blockbuster' Q1 FY27 print (Aug 2026) has drawn fresh attention.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent ~16 of 41 posts (Nov 2022 to Aug 2026). Dhruv_Galada (elevated) did the definitive cycle analysis in 2024 - noted IGPL (a low-cost producer) posting an EBITDA-level loss as a sign the cycle was near capitulation, but also flagged the 1 lakh MT + 1 lakh MT capacity additions by Thirumalai and KLJ as a reason demand would take years to absorb supply, and said he'd wait for a market correction. RK_24, Vineet_Nandwani and Dinesh_476 wrote solid primers (domestic leadership, MAN/BA byproduct economics, import/ADD sensitivity). Recent posts are constructive: Prabhat_Mohanty (elevated, small holding, 'may be biased') - 'worthwhile investment opportunity at present level' for domestic-demand-led investors, expects ADD to be extended, plasticiser from Q2 a margin add; tirth56 and Prabhat then confirmed the ADD was extended for 5 years. Admantium laid out a detailed constructive supply/demand case - 'available at very attractive valuations to play the PAN-OX cycle', Thirumalai lacks balance-sheet strength for a price war.
community_signal: Mild positive lean from an elevated member (Prabhat_Mohanty) with a small, self-described biased holding; Dhruv_Galada's (elevated) earlier detailed view was cautious/wait. No strong high-conviction buy - the recurring caveat is that the key variable (PAN-OX spread) is outside the company's control.
bse_notes: Anti-dumping duty on PAN extended for 5 years (confirmed by company officials on the Aug 2026 concall) - structural positive. New plasticiser plant commissioning, contribution expected from Q2 FY27. Dividend payout maintained at ~260% through the downturn. Import competition and ADD status are the historical swing factors. No SEBI action; no red-flag tier.
bull_case: Lowest-cost domestic PAN producer at a genuine cycle trough (ROCE ~3%, ~1.1x book vs ~3.5x at peak) - operating leverage to any spread recovery
PAN anti-dumping duty extended 5 years; no new domestic PAN capacity expected for 1-2 years; over-levered main competitor
New plasticiser plant starts contributing Q2 FY27 - a fresh margin lever currently only a cost
Near-free MAN and benzoic-acid byproduct streams from PAN wash-water
bear_case: Pure commodity - earnings driven by the PAN-orthoxylene spread and crude, which the company cannot control; ROCE/ROE currently near zero
Global PAN oversupply (China, Taiwan, S. Korea) and depressed MAN prices from Chinese dumping; end-user demand (paints, infra) soft
Domestic capacity additions by Thirumalai and KLJ will take years to be absorbed by ~8% demand growth
Erratic profit history (OPM 5-22%); realistic upside is a 3-5x cyclical recovery, not a structural 10x
verdict_headline: Assigned 10x-in-2-3-years at LOW conviction - a cycle-trough bet on the lowest-cost domestic PAN producer, with the ADD extension and a new plasticiser plant as catalysts; realistically a 3-5x on a spread turn, and the key variable is not in the company's hands
verdict_reasoning: Bucketed as '10x-in-2-3-years' rather than 'neither' under the small/mid-cap recent-catalyst rule: earnings are at a genuine trough, the base is small, and there are two specific, recently-confirmed catalysts (5-year ADD extension, plasticiser plant from Q2 FY27) plus favourable supply dynamics (no new domestic PAN capacity, weak competitor)
Conviction LOW: this is a commodity - PAN-OX spreads and crude drive the P&L and IGPL controls neither; current ROCE/ROE fail the quality gate (as expected at a trough)
Realistic upside is a 3-5x cyclical earnings recovery plus re-rating from ~1.1x toward ~2.5-3x book; the '10x' label is the closest thesis bucket, not a base case
No red-flag tier; no 30-day revisit at LOW conviction. Re-check on PAN-OX spread trend, MAN price recovery, and the plasticiser plant's actual revenue/margin contribution

trusted_signals.note: Small holding, 'may be biased'. Views IGPL as 'a worthwhile investment opportunity at present level' for domestic-demand-led investors: lowest-cost producer, backward+forward integrated, plasticiser from Q2 a margin add, expects (and later confirmed) the ADD would be extended, relatively insulated from US tariffs. Mild positive.

Detailed cycle analysis - low-cost producer posting an EBITDA loss signalled capitulation, but flagged large capacity additions by Thirumalai and KLJ meaning demand would take years to absorb supply; preferred to wait for a broader market correction. Cautious/wait.

four_box.note: ADD extension + no new domestic PAN capacity is real protective tailwind; verdict explicit IGPL 'controls neither' spread/crude (moat=no); re-rating room to book (valuation=yes) but capped at 3-5x (tam=no).

track_record.note: Screener FY18-FY26: rev growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% both cleared in only 2 of 9 (FY18 10%/29%, FY22 68%/21%) - the phthalic-anhydride spread up-cycle years. ROCE swings wildly with PA spreads (45/29/5/29/33/21/5/11/3%); FY26 ROE ~0.2% (deep trough). Cyclical single-product commodity.

quality_metrics.note: Phthalic-anhydride producer at a cyclical trough - ROCE ~3% FY25, ROE ~0.2% FY26; OPM whipsaws with PA spreads (5/10/5% FY24-26). Borrowings Rs362cr FY26 vs ~Rs96cr trough EBITDA (~3.8x). FY26 CFO Rs102cr vs capex Rs89cr (~+15% conversion) - mature assets, capex light - but on depressed EBITDA. Chinese PA oversupply the overhang; capex (maleic anhydride / downstream) yet to earn.
